articles.author: PDF Utils
articles.description:
A while ago I needed to merge two PDFs. Every "free online PDF tool" I found worked the same way: upload your file to someone's server, wait, download the result. A bank statement, a contract, a medical form - straight to a machine I know nothing about, running code I can't see, under a privacy policy I'll never read.
That bothered me enough to build an alternative: PDF Utils (https://yourpdfutils.com/), a set of PDF tools that run entirely in your browser. The file never leaves your device. Not "encrypted in transit", not "deleted after an hour" - it simply never goes anywhere.
Merging, splitting, compressing, rotating, extracting pages, converting images, signing - all of it happens in JavaScript on your machine. When you drop a file on the page, it's read locally, processed locally, and…
articles.title: I built free PDF tools that never upload your files

articles.description:
A software factory is an AI-driven development system that coordinates agents, tools, and automated workflows to turn requirements into working software. Rather than relying on engineers to manually carry out each step, a factory can take an issue through planning, implementation, testing, and review until a pull request is ready. 
More autonomous implementations can also merge and deploy changes with minimal human intervention. But even as more of the development process becomes automated, teams still need to decide how those changes reach users, under what conditions, and with what safeguards. 
As software factories mature and increase delivery throughput, release decisions could become harder to manage at the same pace. Though deploys have become routine, releases have not.

articles.author: Amorizz
articles.description:
I assumed that with an error SDK installed, an async Express route that throws would at least give the user a 500. I had never tested it, so I did. The result surprised me.
The short version: on Express 4, an async handler that throws after an await is reported by Sentry, keeps the process alive, and never answers the request. The client just waits.
Everything below was run on 2026-10-16 on a Linux box with Node 20.19.2, Express 4.22.3, Express 5.3.0 and @sentry/node 11.8.0. The "Sentry server" is a throwaway 15-line Node script on localhost, so nothing leaves the machine. Outputs are pasted from the runs, with log noise trimmed.
Express 4 does not look at the promise your async handler returns. A throw after an await becomes an unhandled rejection, not a next(err) call.
Without an error S…
articles.title: Sentry caught my Express error. The request still hung forever

articles.author: mech.app
articles.description:
Stoke Money replaces the category-based budget with a forward-looking cash flow forecast. Instead of tracking how much you spent on groceries this month, it projects your checking account balance 30 days out, updating the line every time a transaction arrives. The product surfaces a single question: will rent clear on Friday?
This shifts the engineering problem from retrospective categorization to predictive modeling. You need pattern detection that distinguishes recurring bills from one-time purchases, a data structure that represents confidence intervals for future transactions, and a recalculation strategy that keeps forecasts fresh without thrashing on every $5 coffee purchase.
Stoke merges historical transactions and projected events into a single timeline. The ledger is not just a lo…
articles.title: Stoke Money's Cash Flow Forecast Engine: How Real-Time Financial Projections Replace Static Budget Categories

articles.author: Redman WorkflowAlpha
articles.description:
Verdikta : le juge de travail décentralisé


J'ai passé les dernières semaines à chercher comment faire travailler des agents IA sans avoir à leur faire confiance aveuglément. Le problème n'est pas de les faire produire quelque chose — c'est de savoir si ce qu'ils ont produit vaut quelque chose.
Verdikta est un système de primes et d'arbitrage on-chain qui tourne sur Base. Son approche est différente de ce qu'on voit habituellement : l'argent n'est pas envoyé après coup, il est bloqué en séquestre dès le départ, et un jury d'IA note chaque soumission selon une grille d'évaluation publique.
Le créateur de la prime publie une tâche avec un montant en ETH et une grille d'évaluation. Ce montant est placé dans un contrat intelligent — il ne peut ni être annulé ni modifié une fois la tâche ouver…
articles.title: Verdikta : le juge de travail décentralisé qui paie selon des règles connues

articles.author: dev game
articles.description:
Why Hollow Knight Bet on Unity and PlayMaker: The Visual-Scripting Shortcut Behind a 15-Million-Copy Metroidvania


Three developers from Adelaide shipped one of the tightest Soulslike platformers ever made without writing most of its gameplay in code. Team Cherry built Hollow Knight on Unity and built all of its enemies and interactive elements with PlayMaker, a visual-scripting state-machine tool — then sold more than 15 million copies.
That is the short answer to "what engine does Hollow Knight use?" Unity for rendering, physics and ports. PlayMaker for behavior. A handful of custom C# scripts for the parts where feel lives — movement above all.
Most retellings stop at "artists used no-code and won." That misses why the bet worked and where it hurt. My read after digging through Unity's…
articles.title: Why Hollow Knight Bet on Unity and PlayMaker: The Visual-Scripting Shortcut Behind a 15-Million-Copy Metroidvania
